references.text: The Lord tells Moses that he will die on the mountain, just as it says here in Deuteronomy 31:14 that Moses' days are nearing their end.
Joshua is appointed as Moses' successor and given the task of leading the people of Israel, as also described here where Joshua is called forward to receive the Lord's command.
Moses is instructed to give Joshua a command and strengthen him, since Joshua will lead the people across the Jordan – the same transition period described in this verse.
The fulfillment of the prophecy concerning Moses' death that the Lord proclaimed in this verse.
Comparatively, the Lord's presence in the tent of meeting where he spoke with Moses face to face.
After Moses' death, Joshua takes over leadership, as prepared in this verse where the Lord calls Joshua to give him a command.
Moses was faithful throughout God's house as a servant, and Christ as Son over his house – a reflection on Moses' service that concludes with its transfer to Joshua.
